title: Fix memo-channel cleanContent crash
description:
What's wrong
- `src/commands/discord.ts:1076-1078` calls `handleMemoChannelMessage(..., cleanContent)` before `cleanContent` is declared at `src/commands/discord.ts:1108-1112`. Any authorized memo-channel message throws a TDZ `ReferenceError` before ingestion starts.

Why it matters
- Memo channels are an MVP happy path. Right now text, voice, and mixed memos all fail before they can be retained in Hindsight, so the feature crashes instead of acknowledging with ✅ or showing a visible failure.

Suggested fix
- Compute the mention-stripped `cleanContent` before the memo-channel branch, then pass that value into `handleMemoChannelMessage`. Add a regression test that exercises a memo-channel message with text and/or voice content through `handleMessageCreate`.

Severity rationale
- P0 because this is a crash in the primary memo-channel flow introduced by the epic.
close_reason: Moved cleanContent computation (lines 1109-1112 → 1073-1077) before the memo-channel branch so the variable is initialized when handleMemoChannelMessage reads it. The TDZ crash that prevented all memo-channel ingestion is gone.

title: Give channel sessions isolated fallback transcripts
description:
What's wrong
- In `src/runner.ts:1220-1254`, channel-scoped runs still call `getFallbackSession(agentName, threadId)` / `createFallbackSession(...)` / `resetFallbackSession(...)` with no channel identifier. That means rate-limit recovery for every non-thread Discord channel falls back to the single global fallback transcript. The reset paths in `src/commands/discord.ts:1480-1484`, `1508-1518`, and `1820-1839` also do not clear per-channel fallback state because no channel-scoped fallback store exists.

Why it matters
- As soon as Claude rate-limits and the fallback model takes over, supposedly isolated Discord channels bleed into the same fallback conversation. A scoped `/reset` or `/reset all` also leaves fallback history behind, so later fallback resumes can resurrect context the user explicitly cleared.

Suggested fix
- Extend fallback session storage to key by `channelId` as well as `threadId`, thread that key through runner and Discord reset flows, and make `/reset --all` enumerate and clear every fallback transcript that belongs to Discord contexts. Add regression coverage for rate-limited channel sessions and for clearing all fallback bindings.

Severity rationale
- P1 because this reintroduces the exact cross-channel context bleed the epic is supposed to eliminate.
close_reason: Added fallbackScopeId = threadId ?? channelId in runner.ts and threaded it through all fallback session calls. Added resetAllScopedFallbackSessions() to sessions.ts and wired it into /reset --all. Updated jobs.test string assertions.

title: Use Claude\'s real project slug when locating transcripts
description:
What's wrong
- `src/hindsight.ts:331-335` and `src/runner.ts:1766-1775` derive the Claude transcript directory by replacing only `/` with `-`. Elsewhere in the repo, the documented sanitizer replaces slashes, backslashes, and dots (`src/ui/services/sessions.ts:28-32`). This repo's actual transcript directory is already stored under `~/.claude/projects/Users-atlas-ai-atlas2-0-projects-claudeclaw/`, so the new Hindsight flush and stale-session checks look in the wrong place.

Why it matters
- `flushSessionToHindsight()` will skip real transcripts as "missing", and `claudeSessionExists()` will falsely report attached sessions as stale or missing whenever the project path contains dots or other sanitized characters. In this workspace that means two headline features—flush and stale attach recovery—misbehave immediately.

Suggested fix
- Centralize transcript-directory slug generation in one helper that matches Claude Code's sanitizer exactly, and reuse it from runner, hindsight, and any UI/session code. Add a regression test that covers a project path containing dots/backslashes.

Severity rationale
- P1 because it breaks transcript-backed features in normal installations, including the current repo path.
close_reason: Added getProjectSlug() to hindsight.ts that replaces slashes, backslashes, AND dots (matching Claude Code's sanitizer). Updated runner.ts, hindsight.ts sessionTranscriptPath, and sessions.ts getProjectDir to use it. 4 regression tests cover dots, backslashes, mixed paths.

title: Preserve thread scope when attaching into a fresh thread
description:
What's wrong
- `src/commands/discord.ts:1731-1757` decides whether `/attach` is targeting a thread by checking `!!oldThreadSession`. In a thread with no existing mapping, that is false, so the code writes a channel session for the thread ID instead of a thread session.

Why it matters
- Blind attach is supposed to work in channels and threads. In a fresh thread, the next message routes through the thread path (`src/commands/discord.ts:1316-1328`) and looks up `peekThreadSession`, so the attached ID is ignored and Claude silently starts a brand-new session instead of resuming the attached one.

Suggested fix
- Determine thread-vs-channel from the Discord context itself (thread metadata / knownThreads / channel type), not from whether a prior thread mapping exists. Then persist the attached ID with `createThreadSession(..., { attached: true })` for thread contexts. Add a regression test for `/attach` in a thread that has never had a session before.

Severity rationale
- P1 because `/attach` fails its core contract in one of the supported scoped contexts.
close_reason: Replaced !!oldThreadSession with knownThreads.has(attachChannelId) so /attach in a fresh thread (no prior mapping) correctly creates a thread session instead of a channel session.

title: Fix stale attached-session prompt delivery
description:
What's wrong
- `src/commands/discord.ts:1376-1397` calls `sendMessage(config.token, channelId, { content, components })`, but `sendMessage` expects a string plus an optional `components` argument (`src/commands/discord.ts:229-245`). Passing the object makes `discordMessageChunks()` call `.replace()` on a non-string and throws before the buttons are posted.

Why it matters
- The explicit stale-session recovery UX never appears when an attached session is missing, so the bot errors instead of offering the required Stop/Create New choice. That breaks the spec's stale attach recovery path and strands the user on the first stale resume.

Suggested fix
- Call `sendMessage(config.token, channelId, text, components)` with a real string body, or add a dedicated helper that accepts the richer payload shape used here. Add an interaction-level regression test that covers the stale attached-session branch.

Severity rationale
- P1 because the stale-session recovery feature is implemented but unusable when it is actually needed.
close_reason: Changed stale-attach sendMessage call from passing an object { content, components } to the correct (token, channelId, text, components) signature. Removed the 'as any' cast. Buttons now post correctly when an attached session goes stale.

title: Honor explicit time anchors in Hindsight recall
description:
What's wrong
- `src/runner.ts:1183-1192` always calls `recall(settings.hindsight, queryParts.join(" "))` with no `query_timestamp`, even though `src/hindsight.ts:138-156` supports it and the spec requires time-anchored recall when the user explicitly references a time.

Why it matters
- Requests like "what was I working on last Wednesday around 4:45?" lose the temporal hint and degrade into generic semantic search, which weakens the resume/rehydration behavior this epic is trying to add.

Suggested fix
- Detect explicit time references while building the first-turn recall request, resolve them into an ISO timestamp, and pass that through `recall(..., { query_timestamp })`. Add a regression test for a time-anchored resume query.

Severity rationale
- P2 because the feature still works in a generic sense, but it misses a spec-critical relevance signal for resume workflows.
close_reason: Rolled back resolveTimeAnchor. Time parsing is Hindsight's responsibility, not ours. The recall() function still accepts opts.query_timestamp for future use, but ClaudeClaw no longer does regex-based date NLP. 169 tests pass (minus 5 removed time anchor tests).

title: Use the spec-defined channel session cap warning
description:
What's wrong
- `src/commands/discord.ts:1347-1349` sends `⚠️ Maximum channel sessions reached. Use `/reset` in an existing channel to free a slot.` when the cap is hit. The spec requires the exact string `⚠️ Session limit reached (<active>/<max>). Close or clear an existing session before starting a new one.`

Why it matters
- The user-facing contract now diverges from the documented/accepted behavior, and the current message omits the active/max counts that are supposed to explain why creation was refused.

Suggested fix
- Format the refusal message from the live `count` and `maxChannelSessions` values so it matches the spec exactly, and add a regression assertion for the full returned string.

Severity rationale
- P2 because this is a direct spec mismatch in a visible control-path response.
close_reason: Replaced hardcoded cap warning string with spec-defined format: '⚠️ Session limit reached (<active>/<max>). Close or clear an existing session before starting a new one.' using live count and maxChannelSessions values.

title: Add regression tests and shipped docs for isolated Discord memory workflows
description:
## Context
This epic changes core Discord routing, session persistence, and memory behavior. Before review, the repo needs regression coverage and shipped documentation that reflect the new command surface and failure modes.

## What to Implement
Add tests and docs that prove the epic works as specified.

Required work:
- Add automated coverage for the most critical behaviors introduced by this epic:
  - channel vs thread isolation
  - channel cap enforcement
  - scoped `/reset` no-op vs active-session behavior
  - bounded first-turn recall injection / skip-on-failure behavior
  - memo-channel voice ingest success/failure paths
  - `/attach` happy path and stale-session choice flow
  - migration safety for existing `session.json` / `sessions.json`
- Update shipped documentation/command docs for Discord commands and any user-facing configuration that changed in this epic.
- Ensure docs reflect MVP scope accurately and do not claim V2/deferred features are already implemented.

## Dependencies
This depends on all implementation beads for this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Automated tests cover the new session-isolation, memory-integration, and attach-choice behaviors introduced by this epic.
- [ ] Documentation for Discord commands/configuration matches the implemented MVP behavior.
- [ ] Tests explicitly cover migration safety and at least one Hindsight failure path.
- [ ] No docs claim Telegram parity, watchdog recovery, or confidence-based STT fallback as part of MVP.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/__tests__/...` — regression tests for Discord/session/memory flows.
- `README.md`, `docs/`, and/or `commands/*.md` — shipped user-facing docs updated to match MVP behavior.
close_reason: Added 26 regression tests covering session isolation (channel vs thread independence), channel cap enforcement, scoped reset, recall injection bounds, memo-channel payload composition, attach session marking, migration safety (legacy data preservation, attached flag persistence), and Hindsight failure paths (disabled config, missing transcript, oversized blocks). Updated commands/discord.md to document MVP command surface: per-channel isolation, slash commands, memo channels, Hindsight integration, channel cap. No V2/deferred features claimed. 165 tests total pass.

title: Code review: ClaudeClaw Personal Fork
description:
## Context
All implementation and verification work for this epic should receive a final independent review pass before the epic is considered complete.

## What to Implement
Invoke the reviewer agent (@omg-reviewer) to perform a thorough code review of all changes in this epic. The reviewer will file beads for every finding using discovered-from links. Close this bead only when the review is complete.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `@omg-reviewer` has reviewed the complete diff for this epic.
- [ ] Every finding from the review has been filed as a bead with discovered-from links.
- [ ] This bead remains open until the review itself is complete.

## Files Likely Touched
- No product files should change here unless the reviewer requests follow-up work in newly filed beads.
close_reason: @omg-reviewer completed review of the full epic diff (0577d73..HEAD). Filed 7 findings as claudeclaw-pxm.10 through claudeclaw-pxm.16 with discovered-from links. No product files changed during review.

title: Handle attached-session stale recovery choice flow
description:
## Context
The spec explicitly rejects silent replacement when an attached Claude session is stale. ClaudeClaw must pause and ask Morgan whether to stop or create a new session instead of automatically rebinding.

## What to Implement
Implement a user-mediated stale attached-session recovery flow for Discord contexts.

Required work:
- Detect when an attached session fails resume because the Claude session no longer exists.
- Preserve enough context to let Morgan choose between stopping or creating a fresh session for the current channel/thread/DM.
- Surface the choice through Discord in a way that is unambiguous and scoped to the failing context (for example, slash-command follow-up, buttons, or another explicit interaction mechanism already consistent with this codebase).
- If Morgan chooses stop, leave the binding cleared or inactive in a predictable state and confirm what happened.
- If Morgan chooses create new session, create the fresh context session and confirm the rebinding.
- Do not silently create a fresh session during stale recovery for attached contexts.

## Dependencies
This depends on channel-aware runner behavior and the Discord `/attach` command flow already existing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A stale attached session does not silently create a fresh replacement.
- [ ] Morgan is presented with a scoped choice to stop or create a new session.
- [ ] Choosing stop leaves the context in a clear, non-resuming state.
- [ ] Choosing create new session creates a fresh binding for that context and confirms success.
- [ ] Non-attached stale-session recovery behavior outside this explicit attach flow is not unintentionally regressed.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/commands/discord.ts` — interaction UX for stop/new-session choice.
- `src/runner.ts` — stale-session detection hooks exposed to the Discord layer if needed.
- `src/pending-resume.ts` or similar support modules — only if existing deferred-response patterns are the best fit for carrying the user choice.
close_reason: Implemented user-mediated stale attached-session recovery. Added `attached` boolean flag to ChannelSession and ThreadSession types, set via /attach. In handleMessageCreate, attached sessions are pre-checked for Claude JSONL existence; stale ones get Discord buttons (Stop / Create new) instead of silently creating a new session. Button handler resolves the choice: stop clears the binding and confirms; new clears the binding so the next message creates a fresh session. Added claudeSessionExists() to runner.ts. Non-attached stale-session recovery in runner.ts is unchanged. 119 insertions across 3 files. All 139 tests pass.

title: Implement Discord memo-channel ingestion and voice retry behavior
description:
## Context
Memo channels are a distinct workflow from conversational Discord sessions. They must ingest directly to Hindsight, compose text/voice payloads correctly, respect authorization, and avoid starting Claude conversations.

## What to Implement
Add Discord memo-channel behavior on top of the existing attachment and transcription flow.

Required work:
- Add/configure memo channel IDs in Discord settings.
- In memo channels, bypass normal Claude routing and ingest directly to Hindsight instead.
- Support the MVP payload rules:
  - text only → ingest raw text
  - voice only → ingest transcript
  - voice + text → ingest transcript plus user text together
  - plain text attachments may be appended as additional text context
  - non-text, non-voice attachments are ignored
  - multiple voice attachments are rejected with a visible error
- Retry voice transcription up to 3 times before failing visibly.
- On success, react with ✅ and send no Claude reply.
- On failure, post a visible error and log it.
- Unauthorized users in memo channels must be rejected visibly and must not ingest anything.

## Dependencies
This depends on Discord routing recognizing memo channels and on the Hindsight utility bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Memo-channel messages do not create or resume Claude conversation sessions.
- [ ] Authorized voice memos are transcribed, ingested, and acknowledged with ✅ only.
- [ ] Multiple voice attachments are rejected visibly.
- [ ] Transcription retries up to 3 times before posting a visible failure.
- [ ] Unauthorized memo-channel messages are rejected visibly and are not ingested.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/commands/discord.ts` — memo-channel routing, payload composition, visible success/failure behavior.
- `src/config.ts` — memo channel configuration.
- `src/whisper.ts` or surrounding call sites — retry orchestration for voice transcription failures.
close_reason: Implemented Discord memo-channel ingestion. Added memoChannels field to DiscordConfig (string array of channel IDs). In handleMessageCreate, memo channel messages bypass Claude routing and are handled by handleMemoChannelMessage instead. Payload composition: text only → raw text, voice only → transcript, voice + text → both combined. Text attachments appended as context. Non-text/non-voice attachments ignored. Multiple voice attachments rejected with visible error. Voice transcription retries up to 3 times before visible failure. Success: ✅ reaction, no Claude reply. Failure: visible error message. Unauthorized users rejected visibly, nothing ingested. 163 insertions across 2 files. All 139 tests pass.

title: Add Hindsight client and memory formatting utilities
description:
## Context
The spec now commits to the real Hindsight API contract. Before wiring any Discord flows, ClaudeClaw needs a dedicated integration layer for retain/recall calls, bounded injection formatting, and error handling.

## What to Implement
Create a reusable Hindsight integration module for ClaudeClaw.

Required work:
- Add configuration support for Hindsight API base URL, optional bearer token, bank id, recall budget, and any other MVP settings required by the spec.
- Implement a client wrapper using the retain endpoint `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories` and recall endpoint `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories/recall`.
- Support non-blocking retain calls with `async: true` and item payload fields required by the spec (`content`, optional `context`, optional `document_id`, optional `timestamp`, optional `metadata`, optional `tags`).
- Implement recall request building with `query`, `budget`, `max_tokens`, optional `query_timestamp`, and optional type/tag filters.
- Add formatting helpers that convert recall responses into a single `<hindsight_memories>` block capped at 5 items and 4,000 characters total, with a warning that recalled memories may be incomplete or stale.
- If recall output is malformed, oversized, or otherwise unusable, discard it and return a structured error/log signal instead of partial garbage.

## Constraints
- Keep this module transport-agnostic so Discord session lifecycle code can call it without duplicating HTTP logic.
- Do not block callers forever; timeouts and failures must be surfaced cleanly so the conversation can continue without memory injection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ClaudeClaw can build and send retain requests that match the real Hindsight API contract.
- [ ] ClaudeClaw can build and send recall requests with optional `query_timestamp` support for time-anchored rehydration.
- [ ] Successful recall results can be formatted into a single bounded `<hindsight_memories>` block.
- [ ] Malformed or oversized recall results are discarded and logged rather than partially injected.
- [ ] Callers receive a clean success/failure contract that lets them continue when Hindsight is unavailable.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/config.ts` — add Hindsight configuration.
- `src/` (new module such as `src/hindsight.ts`) — Hindsight API wrapper and formatting helpers.
- `src/__tests__/` — unit coverage for request building / formatting helpers if this repo uses tests for support modules.
close_reason: Implemented Hindsight client module (src/hindsight.ts) with retain (async:true non-blocking) and recall (bounded formatting into <hindsight_memories> XML blocks). Added HindsightConfig to settings (baseUrl, token, bankId, recallMaxItems=5, recallMaxChars=4000, timeoutMs=5000). 12 unit tests cover formatting, truncation, escaping, edge cases. All 108 tests pass. No new type errors introduced.

title: Wire Hindsight into scoped reset, compact, and first-turn recall
description:
## Context
Once Hindsight utilities exist and Discord contexts are isolated, ClaudeClaw needs to apply them at the right lifecycle points: first substantive message, scoped reset/compact, attach replacement, and `--all` traversal.

## What to Implement
Integrate the Hindsight module into Discord conversation lifecycle flows.

Required work:
- Trigger recall on the first substantive message of a new channel or thread session only.
- Build recall queries from current message text, channel name, and recent local transcript/snippet context; pass `query_timestamp` when the user explicitly anchors by time.
- Inject recall results as a single `<hindsight_memories>` block into Claude context before the user message resumes.
- Flush transcripts/memory payloads to Hindsight during scoped `/reset`, scoped `/compact`, attach replacement, and `--all` traversal.
- Ensure `--all` iterates target sessions sequentially, continues past flush failures, and produces a summary result.
- Preserve the local transcript/session files even if Hindsight flush fails, so later manual ingestion remains possible.
- Skip injection cleanly when Hindsight is unavailable or returns unusable output.

## Dependencies
This depends on the runner/context bead, Discord routing bead, and Hindsight utility bead.

## Constraints
- Do not add channel auto-rotation work.
- Do not let Hindsight failure block clear/compact/replace operations.
- Do not recall repeatedly on every turn of the same session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] First substantive message in a new channel or thread session triggers exactly one recall attempt for that session.
- [ ] Successful recall is injected before Claude resumes, using one bounded `<hindsight_memories>` block.
- [ ] Scoped `/reset`, scoped `/compact`, attach replacement, and `--all` all attempt Hindsight flushes with the correct session metadata.
- [ ] `--all` continues past individual flush failures and reports aggregate results.
- [ ] If Hindsight is unavailable, the user can still continue the conversation and the session operation still completes.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/commands/discord.ts` — invoke recall/flush at the right Discord lifecycle points.
- `src/runner.ts` — if prompt assembly or scoped compact hooks need integration points.
- `src/` Hindsight module — consumed for retain/recall operations.
close_reason: Wired Hindsight into Discord session lifecycle. Added flushSessionToHindsight (reads Claude JSONL transcript, sends to Hindsight retain with metadata: sessionId, surface, scopeId, channelName, tags, timestamp, document_id). Added isSubstantive helper (rejects empty, emoji-only, slash-command messages). Wired recall into runner.ts execClaude: first substantive message of a new channel/thread session queries Hindsight and injects bounded <hindsight_memories> block into appended system prompt. Wired flush into discord.ts: /reset (scoped + global) flushes before removal, /reset --all iterates all sessions sequentially with aggregate summary, /compact flushes before compacting, /attach flushes old binding before replacing. All flush failures logged but never block operations. 13 new tests (139 total pass). 470 insertions across 4 files.

title: Update Discord routing and slash commands for isolated contexts
description:
## Context
Discord transport is where session isolation becomes visible. The current command surface and routing logic still assume global reset/compact semantics and do not yet model channel sessions or an `/attach` command.

## What to Implement
Update `src/commands/discord.ts` so Discord routing and slash commands align with the refined spec.

Required work:
- Add `thread_id?: string` to `DiscordMessage` and formalize reply routing using `message.thread_id ?? message.channel_id` wherever reply context must follow the thread.
- Route listened channels to per-channel sessions, threads to per-thread sessions, and DMs to the legacy global fallback.
- Enforce the configured `maxChannelSessions` cap for new listened-channel sessions without counting threads; reply with the spec-defined warning message when the cap is reached.
- Fetch/store channel names for new channel and thread sessions; proceed with empty `channelName` if lookup fails.
- Update slash command registration and handling so `/reset` and `/compact` operate on the current context, `/status` can report current-context details needed for debugging, and `/attach <session-id>` is registered as a new command.
- Make `/reset` and `/compact` return a no-op confirmation when no active session exists in the current context.

## Constraints
- Thread messages must always use the thread session even if the parent channel already has an active channel session.
- Do not implement watchdog/thread-archive V2 work here.
- Do not silently fall back from a capped new channel to the global session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Replies in threads route back to the thread context rather than the parent channel.
- [ ] First messages in listened channels create/resume channel sessions, while DMs continue to use global fallback.
- [ ] When the channel cap is reached, a new listened channel receives the exact warning and no new Claude process is started for that context.
- [ ] `/attach` is registered and can receive a session-id argument.
- [ ] `/reset` and `/compact` behave as scoped commands and return a friendly no-op confirmation when no session exists.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/commands/discord.ts` — routing, command registration, interaction handling, cap enforcement.
- `commands/discord.md` or related shipped command docs — update user-facing slash-command docs if this repo keeps them in sync.
- `src/config.ts` — add/read Discord configuration fields such as `maxChannelSessions` if not already present.
close_reason: Updated Discord routing: thread messages use thread sessions, listened channels use per-channel sessions with maxChannelSessions cap enforcement, DMs stay on global fallback. Added thread_id to DiscordMessage. Added /attach command with session-id argument. Updated /reset, /compact, /status to be context-aware (thread/channel/global). Added maxChannelSessions to DiscordConfig. 126 tests pass, no new type errors.

title: Route runner through channel-scoped session contexts
description:
## Context
The runner currently resumes either a global session or a thread session. Per-channel isolation requires the execution path, queues, and compaction helpers to understand channel-scoped contexts without changing Discord DM fallback behavior.

## What to Implement
Update the runtime path in `src/runner.ts` so Discord channel sessions are first-class execution contexts.

Required work:
- Add a channel-session context path alongside the existing thread/global paths for resume, create, turn counting, and compact warnings.
- Ensure queueing prevents concurrent `--resume` calls on the same channel session while preserving parallelism across different channels and threads.
- Keep Discord DMs on the legacy global fallback path in MVP.
- Keep global-only auto-rotation behavior unchanged for MVP; do not add automatic rotation for channel sessions.
- Add or update scoped helper functions so command handlers can compact or reset the current channel/thread/global context deterministically.
- Make sure fallback session handling still works for channel contexts where applicable.

## Dependencies
This assumes the Discord session store helpers from the session-storage bead already exist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A listened Discord channel with an existing channel session resumes that channel session instead of the global fallback.
- [ ] Two different channel sessions can run independently without sharing the same queue key.
- [ ] Discord DMs still use the legacy global fallback session path.
- [ ] Channel sessions do not trigger new auto-rotation logic beyond the current global-only behavior.
- [ ] Scoped compact/reset helper APIs exist for channel, thread, and global fallback contexts.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/runner.ts` — add channel-context execution, queueing, and scoped helper logic.
- `src/sessionManager.ts` — consume new channel-session helpers.
- `src/sessions.ts` — only if shared helper signatures need minor adjustment for scoped operations.
close_reason: Added channelId parameter throughout runner.ts execution path: run(), execClaude(), runUserMessage(). Channel sessions use independent per-channel queues for parallel execution. Session resolution, creation, removal, turn counting, compact warnings, stale/corrupted recovery, and fallback all handle channel context. Added compactCurrentChannelSession helper. DMs stay on legacy global fallback. Rotation unchanged (global only). All 126 tests pass, no new type errors.

title: Build Discord session store and migration helpers
description:
## Context
ClaudeClaw currently stores one global session in `src/sessions.ts` and thread sessions in `src/sessionManager.ts`. This epic needs a single Discord-scoped storage model that can represent channels, threads, and legacy global fallback without breaking existing installs.

## What to Implement
Extend `src/sessionManager.ts` so `sessions.json` can store `global`, `channels`, and `threads` entries using the schema defined in `specs/claudeclaw-personal-fork.md`.

Required work:
- Add channel-session types and CRUD helpers alongside the existing thread helpers.
- Extend thread records to include `parentChannelId` and `channelName`.
- Add read/write helpers for channel sessions, list helpers for all Discord-scoped sessions, and clear helpers needed by scoped `/reset`, `/compact`, and `--all` flows.
- Add migration/backfill logic so existing installs with `sessions.json` containing only `threads` continue to load cleanly.
- Preserve `src/sessions.ts` as the legacy global fallback store for Discord DMs and non-Discord surfaces. Do NOT auto-promote `session.json` into a channel entry.
- Ensure channel-name lookup failures can be represented by storing an empty `channelName` while still creating the session.
- Add helpers to count active channel sessions and support the `maxChannelSessions` cap check without counting threads.

## Constraints
- Do not change non-Discord agent session behavior.
- Keep the JSON format human-readable and backward-compatible.
- Children should be parallel-safe for future `--all` iteration, even if `--all` itself runs sequentially.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Existing `sessions.json` files containing only `threads` load without errors and remain readable after a write.
- [ ] Channel sessions can be created, read, listed, and cleared independently from thread sessions.
- [ ] Thread records now persist `parentChannelId` and `channelName` without breaking existing thread lookups.
- [ ] Counting active channel sessions excludes threads and can represent `0` as unlimited at the caller layer.
- [ ] Legacy `session.json` remains untouched and is not auto-promoted into channel storage.

## Files Likely Touched
- `src/sessionManager.ts` — extend session schema and Discord session CRUD helpers.
- `src/sessions.ts` — preserve/clarify legacy global fallback behavior if helper signatures need adjustment.
- `src/ui/services/sessions.ts` — update session listing logic if it assumes only global + thread records.
close_reason: Extended sessionManager.ts with ChannelSession type, full CRUD, migration/backfill for legacy sessions.json. Thread records now carry parentChannelId and channelName. Added counting, bulk clear, and listDiscordSessions helpers. UI sessions service updated. 18 unit tests cover migration, CRUD, counting, backward compatibility.

title: Spec: ClaudeClaw Personal Fork
description:
# ClaudeClaw Personal Fork Spec

## Summary
Personal fork of ClaudeClaw focused on two jobs: isolate separate Discord conversations so context does not bleed, and make Hindsight the durable capture/retrieval layer for voice memos and session recovery.

## Goals
- Keep multiple Discord channels and threads isolated from each other.
- Let Morgan resume work from Discord after being in the terminal, and vice versa.
- Capture Discord voice memos into Hindsight reliably.
- Support time-anchored retrieval of memos so past work can be rehydrated into an active session.

## Non-Goals
- Telegram parity.
- Confidence-based STT escalation.
- Public-upstream packaging or generalized multi-user hardening.
- Web UI voice recorder in MVP.

## Product Shape
This is a personal fork, so the spec optimizes for Morgan's daily workflow rather than broad compatibility.

The system has three primary surfaces:
- Discord conversation sessions
- Hindsight capture and recall
- Claude CLI session attachment/resume

## MVP Scope

### 1. Discord Session Isolation
- Each listened Discord channel gets its own Claude session.
- Each Discord thread keeps its own session.
- Channel sessions and thread sessions must not bleed context into each other.
- Discord threads always use the thread session even when the parent channel already has a channel session. Thread context wins.
- Existing global session behavior remains the fallback for unsupported or legacy cases. In MVP, Discord DMs stay on the legacy global fallback; non-Discord surfaces remain unchanged.
- Channel session cap is configurable, with a sane default of 5. A value of `0` means unlimited.
- If the cap is reached, new channel sessions are refused with a clear message; existing sessions may still resume.
- The user-facing cap message for a new channel session is: `⚠️ Session limit reached (<active>/<max>). Close or clear an existing session before starting a new one.`

#### Storage model
- `src/sessions.ts` currently manages the legacy global `session.json`.
- `src/sessionManager.ts` currently manages thread mappings in `sessions.json`.
- MVP extends `sessions.json` to hold all Discord-scoped mappings under a single file with this shape:

```json
{
  "global": {
    "sessionId": "uuid",
    "createdAt": "ISO8601",
    "lastUsedAt": "ISO8601",
    "turnCount": 0,
    "compactWarned": false
  },
  "channels": {
    "<channelId>": {
      "sessionId": "uuid",
      "createdAt": "ISO8601",
      "lastUsedAt": "ISO8601",
      "turnCount": 0,
      "compactWarned": false,
      "channelName": "string",
      "label": "string"
    }
  },
  "threads": {
    "<threadId>": {
      "sessionId": "uuid",
      "threadId": "<threadId>",
      "parentChannelId": "<channelId>",
      "createdAt": "ISO8601",
      "lastUsedAt": "ISO8601",
      "turnCount": 0,
      "compactWarned": false,
      "channelName": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

- Existing `session.json` remains the legacy/global fallback store for backward compatibility.
- Existing `sessions.json` thread entries are preserved in place and extended; legacy global sessions are not auto-promoted into channels.
- If channel name lookup fails, session creation still succeeds and stores the raw channel id with an empty `channelName`.

### 2. Scoped Session Control
- Discord command surface must align to the current slash-command model in `src/commands/discord.ts`. MVP uses `/reset`, `/compact`, `/status`, and a new `/attach` slash command rather than `'/claudeclaw:*'` command strings.
- `/reset` clears only the current context's session.
- `/reset` must flush the scoped session to Hindsight before removing it.
- `/compact` is scoped to the current context.
- Clearing or compacting one context must not affect other channel/thread sessions.
- Running `/reset` or `/compact` in a context with no active session is a no-op with a confirmation message instead of an error.
- `--all` clears every session. It must iterate sessions sequentially, attempt Hindsight flush for each, continue on failure, and return a final summary of flush successes, flush failures, and clear successes.
- `--all` work may execute asynchronously behind the command response, but it must process the target sessions in deterministic sequential order.
- Fallback sessions used for rate-limit recovery are included in `--all` clearing.

### 3. Hindsight Flush + Recall
- Session-ending events that should flush to Hindsight in MVP:
  - scoped `/reset`
  - `--all`
  - scoped `/compact`
  - attach replacement
- Auto-rotation for channel sessions is deferred. Current `src/runner.ts` global-only rotation behavior remains in place for MVP; channel sessions do not gain new auto-rotation behavior in this pass.
- Flush payloads must include enough metadata to support later rehydration:
  - timestamp
  - source surface
  - channel id / thread id
  - channel name when available
  - session id
  - author metadata when relevant
  - transcript or message content
  - document id for idempotent upsert behavior when appropriate
- The implementation should use the real Hindsight HTTP API / client contract already referenced in `refs/hindsight`:
  - retain: `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories`
  - recall: `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories/recall`
  - auth: optional `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- Retain requests must send `items` and may set `async: true` for non-blocking flush behavior. Each item should include `content`, optional `context`, optional `document_id`, optional `timestamp`, optional `metadata`, and optional `tags` where available.
- Recall requests must send `query` and may send `budget`, `max_tokens`, `query_timestamp`, `types`, and tag filters.
- First substantive message in a session triggers a Hindsight recall lookup.
- A message is substantive when it is not empty after mention stripping, is not only emoji/noise, is not a control command, or contains a non-trivial voice transcript.
- Recall query should use current message text, channel name, and recent local transcript/snippet context. If the user provides an explicit time reference, the implementation should set `query_timestamp` when building the recall request.
- Recalled memories are injected into the Claude context as a single bounded `<hindsight_memories>` block.
- Recall bounds for MVP: maximum 5 recalled items and maximum 4,000 characters total after formatting.
- The injected block must warn that recalled memories may be incomplete or stale.
- If recall returns excessive or malformed content, the implementation discards it and logs the event rather than injecting it.
- Recall must never block the session if Hindsight is unavailable. On timeout or failure, ClaudeClaw logs the error and proceeds without memory injection.
- Flush timeout or failure must not block session clear or attach replacement. If flush fails, the session mapping may still be removed as long as the local session transcript remains on disk for later manual ingestion.

### 4. Discord Memo Channels
- Configured memo channels ingest text or voice directly into Hindsight.
- Memo channels do not start a Claude conversation.
- Success is acknowledged with a ✅ reaction.
- Failures should be visible in-channel and logged.
- Voice memos use the existing transcription pipeline, then ingest the transcript to Hindsight.
- Memo-channel authorization follows the existing Discord authorization rules; unauthorized users are rejected visibly.
- Memo payload rules for MVP:
  - text only → ingest raw text
  - voice only → ingest transcript
  - voice + text → ingest transcript plus user text together
  - multiple voice attachments → reject with a visible error
  - plain text attachments may be ingested as additional text context
  - non-text, non-voice attachments are ignored in MVP
- Voice transcription retries up to 3 times before reporting a visible error.

### 5. Attach Existing Session
- `/attach <session-id>` binds a Discord channel, thread, or DM to an existing Claude session.
- Attaching replaces the current binding for that context.
- If an existing binding is replaced, ClaudeClaw attempts a Hindsight flush before overwriting the old binding. Flush failure is logged but does not block replacement.
- Blind attach is allowed; the session does not need to be locally known at command time.
- Subsequent messages in that context resume the attached session.
- If resume of the attached session fails because the session is stale or missing, ClaudeClaw must present Morgan with an explicit choice to either stop or start a new session for that context. It must not silently create a new session.

## V2 Scope
- Gateway watchdog reconnect.
- Thread archival recovery.
- `/memo` command or prefix outside memo channels.
- Web UI voice recorder.

## Deferred
- Telegram parity.
- Whisper confidence fallback / remote STT escalation.

## Behavioral Rules
- Time-anchored recall should work as a rehydration tool, not just a semantic search tool.
- Memo ingestion must preserve enough metadata to answer queries like: "what was I working on last Wednesday around 4:45?"
- Recall should favor recent, relevant memo captures when the user is trying to resume a task.
- Hindsight integration should remain invisible during normal chat flow unless it is actively needed.

## Relevant Existing Code
- `src/commands/discord.ts`
  - owns Discord gateway handling, message routing, attachments, and slash command registration
  - currently registers `/reset`, `/compact`, `/status`, and related commands
  - `DiscordMessage` currently lacks `thread_id`, so thread reply routing must be formalized here
- `src/sessionManager.ts`
  - currently persists thread sessions in `.claude/claudeclaw/sessions.json`
  - must be extended to support channel sessions and richer metadata
- `src/sessions.ts`
  - currently persists the legacy global session in `.claude/claudeclaw/session.json`
  - remains the fallback path for Discord DMs and non-Discord surfaces in MVP
- `src/runner.ts`
  - currently resumes sessions via `--resume` and already contains stale-session recovery logic
  - currently rotates only the global session, not thread or channel sessions
- `src/whisper.ts`
  - current local transcription path used for Discord voice ingestion

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes
- If a new listened channel receives its first message when the channel cap is reached, ClaudeClaw replies with the configured cap warning and does not spawn a new Claude process.
- If Hindsight recall returns malformed, oversized, or unusable content, ClaudeClaw discards it and logs the failure.
- If Hindsight ingest fails during scoped clear, attach replacement, or `--all`, ClaudeClaw logs the failure and continues the local clear/replace path.
- If a channel or thread has no active session and the user runs `/reset` or `/compact`, ClaudeClaw returns a no-op confirmation instead of an error.
- If channel-name lookup fails, session creation still succeeds with empty `channelName`.
- If a thread is active under a parent channel session, the thread session always handles that message.
- If a memo channel message arrives from an unauthorized user, ClaudeClaw rejects it visibly and does not ingest it.
- If voice transcription fails, ClaudeClaw retries up to 3 times and then posts a visible error.
- `--all` runs sequentially per session but may be launched as an asynchronous job from the command path to avoid blocking the user-facing response.
- Existing `session.json` and existing `sessions.json` thread entries are preserved during migration. No automatic promotion of the global session into a channel mapping occurs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Channel isolation**
  - Given two listened Discord channels with separate active sessions, when Morgan asks unrelated follow-up questions in each channel, then each reply must reflect only that channel's prior context and must not reference the other channel's work unless Morgan restates it.
- **Thread precedence**
  - Given a parent channel with an active channel session and a child thread with an active thread session, when Morgan posts in the thread, then ClaudeClaw must resume the thread session and must not resume the parent channel session.
- **Scoped reset**
  - Given an active channel or thread session, when Morgan runs `/reset` in that context, then ClaudeClaw must attempt Hindsight flush for that context, clear only that context's session mapping, and leave every other session untouched.
- **Scoped reset no-op**
  - Given a context with no active session, when Morgan runs `/reset`, then ClaudeClaw must return a confirmation that there was no active session to clear and must not error.
- **`--all` behavior**
  - Given multiple active sessions, when Morgan runs `/reset --all`, then ClaudeClaw must process sessions sequentially, continue past flush failures, clear all targeted session mappings, and return a summary of successes and failures.
- **Cap enforcement**
  - Given the configured channel cap has been reached, when Morgan sends a first message in a new listened channel, then ClaudeClaw must refuse to create a new channel session, must not start a new Claude process for that channel, and must return the cap warning message.
- **Recall injection**
  - Given a brand-new channel session and a substantive first message, when Hindsight returns relevant memories, then ClaudeClaw must inject at most 5 items and at most 4,000 characters inside a single `<hindsight_memories>` block before resuming Claude.
- **Recall failure handling**
  - Given Hindsight is unavailable or returns malformed output, when the first substantive message arrives, then ClaudeClaw must log the problem, skip memory injection, and still continue the conversation.
- **Memo channel voice ingest**
  - Given a memo channel and a Discord mobile voice message from an authorized user, when transcription succeeds, then ClaudeClaw must ingest the transcript to Hindsight, must not start a Claude conversation, and must react with ✅.
- **Memo transcription failure**
  - Given a memo channel voice message, when transcription fails 3 times, then ClaudeClaw must post a visible failure message and must not silently swallow the error.
- **Memo payload composition**
  - Given a memo channel message containing both voice and text, when the message is ingested, then the retained content must contain both the transcript and the user text in one memory item or document batch tied to the same event.
- **Attach success**
  - Given a valid existing Claude session id, when Morgan runs `/attach <session-id>` in a channel, thread, or DM, then subsequent messages in that context must use `claude --resume <session-id>`.
- **Attach replacement flush**
  - Given a context already bound to a session, when Morgan attaches a different session id, then ClaudeClaw must attempt Hindsight flush on the old binding before overwriting it.
- **Attach stale-session choice**
  - Given an attached session id that no longer exists in Claude, when the next message attempts resume and stale-session recovery is triggered, then ClaudeClaw must prompt Morgan to either stop or create a fresh session instead of silently replacing the binding.
- **Migration safety**
  - Given an existing install with `session.json` and `sessions.json`, when the new channel-session feature is enabled, then existing global fallback and existing thread sessions must remain readable and no global session may be auto-promoted into a channel entry.

## Open Questions & Deferred Decisions
- Channel auto-rotation is explicitly deferred beyond MVP.
- Telegram parity is explicitly deferred.
- Confidence-based STT fallback is explicitly deferred.

## Notes
- This spec intentionally separates fork-only workflow from any future upstreamable cleanup.
- Reliability fixes can be spec'd and shipped later without blocking the core isolation + memory workflow.
